C1.note: Provider tool ids are preserved through native assistant tool_use and user tool_result blocks.

C2.note: Tool definitions stay stable and each native action/observation pair is appended without rewriting history.

C3.note: Large observations become run-scoped artifacts with head/tail previews and bounded range reads.

C4.note: Context over budget is automatically summarized by the fast model while recent native blocks and persisted run evidence remain.

D1.note: The run driver is an application task independent of the SSE subscriber.

D2.note: Runs execute independently of subscribers and running work is scanned on API startup.

D3.note: Persisted native action/result blocks rebuild model context after restart; unobserved side effects stop as incomplete instead of unsafe retry.

P1.note: Multi-step work has a validated plan tool, update events, and end-of-context recitation.

P2.note: Plans track step state and budget exhaustion is explicit; arbitrary user completion assertions are not yet machine-bound.

P3.note: Create/publish use projection read-back; push/dispatch verify durable delivery events and recipient hashes.

P4.note: Tool errors remain in the next model observation.

P5.note: A tool is disabled after three consecutive failures.

M1.note: Run input and campaign memory persist, but follow-up chat still sends full history.

M2.note: Each run owns a durable, tenant-scoped artifact workspace.

M3.note: Explicitly approved org preferences persist across sessions, are PII-redacted, injectable, and deletable.

S1.note: Same-turn independent tool calls execute concurrently.

S2.note: Read-only subagents use isolated context/budget/tool allowlists and return only a bounded summary plus step metadata.

G1.note: Every mutating tool enters Harness policies; outward actions additionally stop at a durable confirmation boundary.

G2.note: Risky actions create tenant-scoped pending confirmations; the durable run pauses and continues only after approval.

G3.note: REST tool dependencies are scoped by authenticated org and author.

X1.note: SSE emits structured tool_call, tool_result, tool_error, and done events.

X2.note: The live run surface shows the execution plan, tool phases, independent verification outcomes, confirmation gates, and terminal state.

X3.note: The UI stores the active run id, restores its original turns after refresh, replays events from sequence zero, then reconnects from the last accepted monotonic cursor without duplicating work.

X4.note: Per-turn/cumulative tokens, LLM latency, elapsed time, and failures persist in the run trace; normalized provider cost remains.

X5.note: Completion, failure, and incomplete handoffs are distinct; the durable run id, completed tool evidence, verification results, and remaining incomplete state stay visible.
